content.title: Signaling Proposal: Recovery and PHOTON Conversion of Dormant ATONE Airdrop Allocations
content.description:
# Signaling Proposal: Recovery and PHOTON Conversion of Dormant ATONE Airdrop Allocations



## Abstract



This proposal asks the AtomOne community to consider a mechanism for addressing original ATONE airdrop allocations that have remained completely inactive since distribution approximately two years ago.



The objective is to improve ATONE staking participation and strengthen the network's economic security by addressing a portion of the ATONE supply that was distributed to wallets but has never been put to use through transfers, staking, delegation, or governance participation.



Under the proposed approach, only verifiably identifiable original airdrop allocations that have remained untouched since distribution would be eligible for consideration. Before any conversion, affected holders would receive a final three-month period in which to move, stake, delegate, or otherwise demonstrate control and active use of their ATONE.



If an allocation remains untouched after that notice period, the community could consider authorizing its conversion into PHOTON under a transparent, technically and legally reviewed mechanism.



This is a signaling proposal only. It does not itself authorize or execute changes to account balances.



## Rationale



The original ATONE airdrop took place approximately two years ago. Holders have therefore already had a substantial period in which to access their allocations, move their tokens, stake, delegate, or participate in governance.



However, some original airdrop allocations appear to remain entirely untouched in their recipient wallets. These inactive allocations contribute to the amount of ATONE that remains unlocked and outside the staking economy.



A low staking ratio can weaken the network's economic security. When a significant amount of ATONE remains unlocked and is not bonded to validators, a smaller proportion of the total supply is actively contributing to proof-of-stake security and participating in the network's governance.



ATONE is the network's staking and governance asset. Holding ATONE without ever using it for staking or governance provides no direct contribution to these functions. The proposal therefore seeks to distinguish between holders who actively use their ATONE and allocations that have remained dormant since the airdrop.



The intention is not to penalize people for being inactive or to take away value arbitrarily. Instead, it is to explore whether demonstrably unused original airdrop allocations could be converted into PHOTON.



This could offer a mutually beneficial outcome:



- **For the network:** reduce the amount of dormant, unlocked ATONE originating from unused airdrop allocations and create an opportunity to improve the staking ratio and economic security.

- **For inactive holders:** preserve value in PHOTON rather than leaving an unused ATONE allocation in a wallet that does not participate in staking or governance.

- **For active holders and validators:** support a healthier staking economy in which a greater proportion of circulating ATONE is actively contributing to network security.



The underlying principle is straightforward: ATONE should serve its purpose as the network's staking and governance asset. Holders who do not wish to participate in those functions could retain value through PHOTON instead.



## Proposed Mechanism



The community is asked to consider the following framework:



### 1. Identify eligible dormant allocations



Eligibility would be limited to original ATONE airdrop allocations that can be independently and verifiably identified.



An allocation would qualify for consideration only if reliable on-chain records establish that:



- The ATONE originated from the original airdrop.

- The relevant allocation has remained in its original recipient wallet.

- There has been no outgoing movement or other qualifying on-chain activity involving that allocation since distribution.

- The allocation has not been transferred, staked, delegated, or used in governance.



The eligibility assessment must distinguish original airdrop allocations from ATONE subsequently acquired by the same wallet through other means.



### 2. Provide a final three-month notice period



Before any conversion is implemented, eligible wallets must receive a clearly announced three-month period to demonstrate that their holders wish to retain and use their ATONE.



During this period, holders could:



- Transfer their ATONE to another wallet.

- Stake or delegate their ATONE.

- Participate in governance.

- Perform another clearly defined qualifying on-chain action.



Any qualifying activity during the notice period would remove the affected allocation from consideration for conversion.



The notice period should be publicly communicated through official AtomOne channels and include clear instructions explaining how holders can preserve their ATONE.



### 3. Convert only allocations that remain dormant



After the three-month period, only allocations that still meet all eligibility requirements would be considered for conversion.



The conversion must use a transparent, community-approved ATONE-to-PHOTON formula. The exact conversion mechanism, supply treatment, accounting, and technical implementation must be determined through a separate review and approval process.



No conversion should occur automatically as a consequence of this signaling proposal.



### 4. Publish transparent eligibility and conversion records



Before implementation, the community should be provided with:



- The methodology used to identify eligible original airdrop allocations.

- The total amount of ATONE potentially eligible for conversion.

- The criteria used to determine whether an allocation remained dormant.

- The final three-month notice and exclusion process.

- The proposed conversion formula and its supply implications.

- A verifiable record of any conversions ultimately authorized.



## Implementation Requirements



If the community supports this direction, developers and relevant contributors should investigate the technical and legal feasibility of the mechanism.



Any implementation must include:



- Reliable identification of original airdrop allocations.

- A method of distinguishing dormant airdrop allocations from other funds.

- A clear definition of qualifying activity.

- A publicly verifiable three-month notice period.

- Protection against mistakenly including active holders or unrelated ATONE balances.

- A transparent and auditable conversion process.

- Appropriate technical, constitutional, and legal review.

- A separate governance authorization or other required approval before any account balances or token supplies are changed.



## Safeguards



This proposal must not be interpreted as authorization to confiscate or modify any holder's balance immediately.



The following safeguards are essential:



1. Only demonstrably traceable original airdrop allocations may be considered.

2. ATONE acquired independently of the original airdrop must not be affected.

3. Any qualifying activity during the three-month notice period must exclude the relevant allocation from conversion.

4. Holders must have a reasonable and publicly communicated opportunity to preserve their ATONE.

5. The conversion formula and its economic consequences must be disclosed before implementation.

6. The mechanism must be independently auditable and subject to the required governance and legal approvals.

7. No balances may be modified solely as a result of this signaling proposal.



## Requested Community Decision



This proposal asks the AtomOne community to express its support or opposition to the following principle:



**Should the AtomOne community investigate and, subject to all required approvals, implement a mechanism to convert original ATONE airdrop allocations that have remained completely untouched since distribution into PHOTON, after providing their holders with a final three-month opportunity to demonstrate activity and retain their ATONE?**



The primary objective is to improve ATONE staking participation and strengthen the network's economic security by reducing the amount of permanently dormant, unlocked ATONE originating from unused airdrop allocations.



Holders who wish to participate in the network's staking and governance economy should have the opportunity to retain their ATONE. Holders who do not wish to participate should have the opportunity to retain value through PHOTON.



The goal is a healthier staking economy, stronger network security, and a more productive use of the assets distributed through the original airdrop.

proposals.title: AtomOne v4 Upgrade
proposals.summary:
# AtomOne v4 upgrade

The AtomOne v4 release is a major release that will follow the standard
governance process. The on-chain voting period will last 3 weeks.

On governance vote approval, validators will be required to update the AtomOne
chain binary at the halt-height specified in the on-chain proposal.

A full technical reference for the v4 release is published at
[atom.one/blog/atomone-v4-technical-reference](https://atom.one/blog/atomone-v4-technical-reference/)
and is the recommended companion to this proposal.

## Release Binary & Upgrade Resources

IMPORTANT: Note that AtomOne v4.0.0 binary MUST be used.

The release can be found [here](https://github.com/atomone-hub/atomone/releases/tag/v4.0.0).
The changelog can be found [here](https://github.com/atomone-hub/atomone/blob/v4.0.0/CHANGELOG.md#v400).

## Proposed Release Contents

This release introduces the following major new features:

- Adopt the AtomOne SDK (`github.com/atomone-hub/cosmos-sdk`, versioned
  `v0.500.1` and based on Cosmos SDK v0.50) as the canonical home for all
  AtomOne-specific governance, staking and fee-market logic, on a release
  trajectory independent from the Cosmos SDK
- Upgrade to IBC-go v10, and CometBFT v0.38
- Introduce **Governors** (ADR-006): a new class of governance participants
  that allows ATONE stakers to delegate governance voting power independently
  from staking, addressing the participation gap created by the Constitution's
  prohibition on validators inheriting delegator votes
- Add the **`x/coredaos`** module, translating the constitutional Steering DAO
  and Oversight DAO into enforceable on-chain capabilities (proposal
  endorsement, annotation, voting-period extension, and constitutional veto)
- Set validator commission to a network-enforced fixed rate of **5%** and
  introduce the **Nakamoto Bonus** reward mechanism (ADR-004), starting at
  η = 3%, to improve stake decentralization
- Migrate the governance module from the `atomone.gov.v1` Protobuf namespace
  to `cosmos.gov.v1`, with a backward-compatibility wrapper preserving all
  pre-existing `atomone.gov.v1` query and message endpoints throughout the v4
  lifecycle (the wrapper is scheduled for removal in v5)
- Migrate `x/dynamicfee` into the AtomOne SDK, with a fix for the unlimited
  block-gas (`MaxGas = -1`) edge case
- Add the **`10-gno`** IBC light client, enabling future IBC connectivity with
  Gno chains running Tendermint2 and laying the groundwork for the
  Validation-as-a-Service shared-security model
- Backport consensus key rotation

The other changes can be found in the AtomOne binary changelog [here](https://github.com/atomone-hub/atomone/blob/v4.0.0/CHANGELOG.md#v400)
as well as the AtomOne SDK changelog [here](https://github.com/atomone-hub/cosmos-sdk/blob/v0.500.1/CHANGELOG.md#v05000---2026-06-22).

## Schedule

With a three-week voting period, in the event the proposal is supported, it
should pass around Jul 15th. The upgrade will be expected to take place the
following week, at Jul 22th. The specific block halt-height is [9,550,000](https://www.mintscan.io/atomone/block/9550000).

## Testing and Testnets

The v4 release has gone through rigorous testing, including e2e tests and
integration tests. The AtomOne v4 upgrade was also subjected to a security
audit carried out by [Oak Security](https://oaksecurity.io/). The full report
is available at
[github.com/atomone-hub/atomone/tree/main/docs](https://github.com/atomone-hub/atomone/blob/main/docs/v4%20-%20Oak%20Audit%20Report.pdf).

Validators and node operators have joined a [public testnet](https://testnet.explorer.allinbits.services/atomone-testnet-1)
to participate in a test upgrade to a release candidate before the AtomOne
network upgrades to the final release.

## Potential risk factors

Although very extensive testing and simulation will have taken place there
always exists a risk that the AtomOne experiences problems due to potential
bugs or errors from the new features. In the case of serious problems,
validators should stop operating the network immediately. Coordination with
validators will happen in the #validator-private channel of the AtomOne
Community Discord to create and execute a contingency plan. Likely this will
be an emergency release with fixes or the recommendation to consider the
upgrade aborted and revert back to the previous release of AtomOne (v3.3.0).

## Governance votes

The following items summarize the voting options and what it means for this
proposal:

YES - You agree that the AtomOne chain should be updated with this release.
NO - You disagree that the AtomOne chain should be updated with this release.
ABSTAIN - You wish to contribute to the quorum but you formally decline to vote
either for or against the proposal.
